trigger: doc-repo-f9 relayed a finding from legacy-design-tools-shared-reader: apps/property-explorer/src/lib/live-envelope-augment.ts has ZERO callers in hauska-map main, discovered while that lane was answering a side question about whether the live map draws real setback polygons independent of atom backfill.

correction.originalClose_impliedImpact: The original close doc presented PR #362 (live-envelope-augment.ts's applyLiveDeriveToFacets now reconciling against the atom chain's reported area) as closing PE's side of the boundary-envelope atom program's item 2. That framing did not state whether the fixed function is actually reachable from any real user-facing path — an omission, not a false statement, but one that reads as more impactful than verified.
correction.verifiedNow: Repo-wide search for the actual function names (not just the file path) confirms augmentFacetsWithLiveEnvelope / fetchLiveEnvelopeDerive / applyLiveDeriveToFacets have no caller anywhere in hauska-map outside their own test file. The only real consumer of anything in live-envelope-augment.ts is fact-sheet-resolver.ts, which imports solely the boolean predicate facetsNeedLiveEnvelopeDerive and uses it to REFUSE (mark the PDF/sheet envelope atom_path_pending) rather than to invoke the live-derive path — a deliberate design per that file's own comment ("Live derive is not a buildable-envelope atom... must not print a lot-percentage from the side door"). Also checked: no map/browse component reads envelope.geojson anywhere in the app. InspectCard.tsx and parcel-lookup.ts each carry their own comments documenting that they used to run an independent live-envelope fetch/merge and were deliberately cut back to a single source (fact-sheet-resolver.ts) after running duplicate paths produced a real bug (one X-ray PDF printing two different zones on two different sheets).
correction.classification: Per doc_repo/ENFORCEMENT.md's "mechanisms must be armed and fed": this is a dormant mechanism, not a starved one — the logic is correct and the gating precondition (a real atom-derived area to reconcile against) would be populated correctly if it ran, but nothing triggers it today. Dormant reports as success the same way a real fix does; this addendum exists so that distinction isn't lost.
correction.whatIsStillTrue: The fix itself is not wrong or wasted: it is correct, tested in isolation, mirrors legacy-design-tools' own now-live reconcileAtomEnvelope.ts exactly, and is ready the moment something calls the wrapper — but it is not affecting any real user-facing rendering today, and should not be cited as having closed a live-serving gap.

selfCriticism: Should have traced the caller graph of live-envelope-augment.ts before fixing it, not after a peer caught it in an unrelated side question. The mission brief that prompted this card was itself corrected once already (McLennan misattribution, see the original close doc) for an unverified claim; this is a second instance in the same card of insufficient verification before reporting done — this time by me, not a peer's brief. Escalating explicitly rather than only fixing it quietly.
openQuestion_notDecidedHere: Whether the correct next step is wiring augmentFacetsWithLiveEnvelope into a real caller (if the map/card is still meant to draw a live-derived envelope polygon independent of the atom-chain's baked geometry-less facets), or retiring the function outright (if the single-source fact-sheet-resolver.ts model already superseded the need for it, per ENFORCEMENT's "retirement is proven by decline, never by documentation" — meaning if it should be retired, that needs an actual decline path added, not just leaving it unreferenced). Routed to doc-repo-2c; not decided unilaterally by this lane.
